title: Argentina's Monetary Report Card: Promise versus Delivery under Milei
standfirst: Javier Milei won by promising to abolish the central bank and scrap the peso. He kept neither, and now runs the most hands-on monetary regime in the hemisphere. Inflation still collapsed, from 25 percent a month to near 2. The revolution he sold did not do it. A budget surplus propped up by elections and borrowed dollars did, lashed to an exchange-rate band that floats on the very inflation it is meant to kill. The win is real. Nothing makes it last.
author: Nik Khosravipour

close.verdict: Delivered: the disinflation from 25.5 % to 2.1 % per month, the parallel premium from triple digits to near parity, a fiscal surplus held every month since January 2024. Reversed: dollarization and the closure of the central bank. Held by discretion: the surplus and a reserve position negative on net. Nothing locks the achievement in.
